name: claudeignore-guard
description: Makes `.claudeignore` work, and enforces `.gitignore` alongside it by default. Claude Code has no native .claudeignore (anthropics/claude-code#579, #4160, #29455) yet blog posts teach it as if it did, so people list .env there and believe they are protected while nothing reads the file. This PreToolUse hook enforces both on Read/Edit/Write/NotebookEdit: an excluded path is denied, and the denial names the exact file and line of the rule plus the '!' line that would allow it. Symlinks are resolved, so a link to an excluded file is denied too. .gitignore is merged in by default so a repo that already keeps secrets out of git is protected with no per-project setup; .claudeignore rules are applied LAST and always win on conflict. Matching is git's own: each directory's ignore files are concatenated into a scratch mirror and queried with `git check-ignore`, so gitignore semantics (negation, anchoring, **, dir-only rules, nested files, precedence) are exact rather than re-implemented, paths that do not exist yet are answered, and the project need not be a git repository. The mirror lives in a per-user 0700 directory keyed by a 64-bit hash, carries a README naming its project, and refuses a base owned by anyone else; if it cannot be built the hook SAYS SO rather than silently allowing everything (CLAUDEIGNORE_STRICT=1 denies instead). Freshness uses cp -p .track copies and a bidirectional mtime gate — no cache TTL to tune. Does NOT cover Bash or Grep, and on Claude Code 2.1.220 permissions.deny was measured not to cover them either (see docs/GOTCHAS.md); the sandbox is the only mechanism that constrains processes rather than tools. Requires git. Env: CLAUDEIGNORE_DISABLED=1, CLAUDEIGNORE_NO_GITIGNORE=1, CLAUDEIGNORE_MODE=warn, CLAUDEIGNORE_QUIET=1, CLAUDEIGNORE_STRICT=1.
